clue.text: Doctor wears campaign medal in clothing store

parts.note: a military campaign is a war
the OBE is a British honour, worn as a medal

explanation.surface: A doctor puts on his campaign medal while standing in a shop that sells clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardrobe is a cupboard where garments are kept, a store for clothing.

explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic Sea is a body of sea water in northern Europe.

clue.text: Music and endless fun in the London area

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun

explanation.walkthrough: Poplar is a district in the East End of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Poplar is a district of East London, so it names an area of the capital.

clue.text: Son on time to start with nudges actor?

indicators.note: the phrase for on time comes first, with the son after it

parts.note: prompt means punctual, on time

clue.text: Irishman with anger about appearing in supporting role

parts.note: Pat, short for Patrick, is a stock Irish name

parts.note: rage is anger
an act that is on is appearing on stage

clue.text: Fibre replaced Lycra in crop tops

indicators.note: the letters of Lycra are put back in a different order
the tops, first letters, of in and crop

explanation.surface: A synthetic fibre has taken the place of Lycra in cropped tops.

clue.text: Hotel chain needs houses

indicators.note: the words chain needs contain, or house, the answer within their letters

explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a place offering lodging to travellers, an old-style hotel.

clue.text: Triple-echo interfered with surveillance equipment?

indicators.note: something interfered with has been tampered with, so these letters are jumbled

clue.text: Student attire bringing French fashion into English clubs?

indicators.note: the French word for fashion is put into the letters for English clubs

parts.note: clubs is one suit in a pack of cards
ton is French for style or fashion, as in bon ton

explanation.walkthrough: An Eton suit is the short jacket and trousers once worn by pupils of Eton, the English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eton suit was the formal uniform of schoolboys at Eton College, so it is clothing for a pupil.

clue.text: Servile follower duke engaged in Dorset town

indicators.note: the duke is busy inside, so his letter sits within the town

explanation.walkthrough: Poole is a coastal town in Dorset, a county of south-west England.

clue.text: With effort carry round pole — getting breather

indicators.note: the word for carrying goes round the pole, enclosing it

parts.note: to lug is to carry something heavy with effort
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: Hauling a pole around, someone stops for a breather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breather' looks like a rest; here it is the organ that breathes.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ that draws in air is literally the thing in the body that breathes.

clue.text: Irregular mostly out to install Left?

definitions.text: Irregular mostly out to install Left?

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left is put inside the scrambled letters
letters that are out are disordered, so they are rearranged
most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: An irregular fighter is usually out to put a left-wing regime in power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last R of Irregular; 'out' rearranges IRREGULA into GUERRILA, and 'to install' puts L into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Guerrillas are irregular soldiers, and many insurgencies have aimed to bring left-wing governments to power.

clue.text: Son is in a position to give help

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the son and is sit in the phrase meaning a position

parts.note: a stance is a position or posture
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Son is in a position' reads as a plain sentence; each word is a building block, with 'in' the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance is the aid or support given to someone, the same as help.

clue.text: Generally where schools are located?

definitions.meaning: on the whole, for the most part
schools of fish swim in the sea, poetically called the main

explanation.surface: Where, in general, are schools to be found?
explanation.walkthrough: 'schools' suggests education; it means shoals of fish, and the main is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means mostly or on the whole, and literally places fish shoals in the ocean.

clue.text: Note in enclosure kept secret a tasty morsel

parts.note: enc. is the abbreviation for enclosure on a letter

indicators.note: the musical note goes in the word for kept secret

la is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a tortilla rolled round a savoury filling, a Mexican snack.

clue.text: Organisation taking role in recycled energy?

recycled material is made into something new, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a part is a role in a play

explanation.walkthrough: 'recycled' rearranges the letters of energy into GREENY, and the role is set inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Green Party is a political organisation campaigning on environmental issues.

clue.text: Savoury dish, lightly cooked, cut into

parts.note: rare meat is lightly cooked
bit is the past tense of bite, cutting into with teeth

explanation.surface: A savoury dish, only lightly cooked, gets cut into.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is a British dish of cheese sauce melted on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarebit is melted cheese on toast, a savoury dish served hot.

clue.text: Staff coming around, but this would require filling

parts.note: a pole is a staff or stick
tho, short for though, means but

clue.text: Impressive eastern prince seen occasionally

indicators.note: only some of the letters of prince are seen, every other one

explanation.surface: An eastern prince makes a grand impression on his rare appearances.
explanation.definitionFit: Something epic is grand and heroic in scale, so it is impressive.

clue.text: High-ranking ecclesiastic not yet dead, can one infer?

parts.note: pre means before, so not yet
the late someone is a dead person

explanation.surface: A senior churchman is still alive, one may deduce.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks about someone's health; 'can one infer?' flags that the answer splits into before and deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a bishop or other senior cleric of high rank.

clue.text: Spooky group keeping people up in House of Usher?

indicators.note: the spy agency keeps the people inside it

parts.note: the CIA is an agency of spooks, or spies

explanation.walkthrough: The Fall of the House of Usher is a Poe story; here an usher shows people to seats in a picture house.
explanation.definitionFit: Ushers guide film audiences to their seats, so a picture house is a place where ushers work.

clue.text: Droll nonsense — could it bring the house down?

definitions.text: could it bring the house down?

parts.note: dry humour is droll, wry and understated
rot is rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: Witty nonsense that brings the house down with laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring the house down' suggests a comedy triumph; literally it is a fungus rotting a building's timbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a fungus that decays the timber of buildings, which can eventually make them collapse.

clue.text: Drink one to limit bone disease

indicators.note: the drink and one bound the bone on both sides, enclosing it

parts.note: beer is a drink
a rib is a bone
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.definitionFit: Beriberi is a disease caused by a lack of vitamin B1.

clue.text: Not well, turned to tuck into simple food options

ill means not well
milk that has turned has gone off

explanation.surface: Feeling unwell, someone turns to plain food to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill of fare is a menu, listing the dishes a restaurant offers.

clue.text: Ottoman officer edges away from infidel

parts.note: a pagan is a non-believer, an infidel

clue.text: British planes on time in southeast make low attack

indicators.note: the time and planes go within the compass direction's letters

indicators.note: the planes come on, after, the time in this across clue

parts.note: the RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force

explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack ground targets with gunfire from low-flying aircraft.

clue.text: Artist took the stage, being filmed
